findings.headline: Pricing page says you never switch analytics off. Terms allow suspension.
findings.explanation: The terms also add a first-month trigger the FAQ never mentions, and an account left suspended two months can be deleted with no refund.

claim_a.quote: We'll never turn your analytics off for occasional traffic spikes or if a payment fails the first time

claim_b.quote: In the event you fail to upgrade your account within seven days of our request, we reserve the right to suspend your account and restrict your use of our Services anytime after the seventh day following our notice to you.

findings.why_not_just_wording: Never turn your analytics off and reserve the right to suspend your account describe opposite outcomes for the same customer.
findings.caveat: The terms describe a right you may never use and the FAQ describes what you actually do. Dropping the word never would close it.

findings.headline: Pricing page sells full API access. The $19 to $399 ladder is elsewhere.
findings.explanation: 600 an hour is Tier 1 of six. The top tier costs nearly nine times the $45 plan it sits on.

claim_a.quote: Full API access with 600 requests per hour included.

claim_b.statement: Up to $399 a month for more

findings.why_not_just_wording: The pricing page names no price for API capacity while another page prices it in six steps.
findings.caveat: 600 requests an hour is generous and most customers stay on Tier 1. The word Full is doing the work in a list that otherwise advertises no extra fees.

findings.headline: Event tracking has no extra fees, but events count as pageviews.
findings.explanation: Your price is set entirely by monthly pageviews, so heavy event tracking moves a customer into a higher band.

claim_a.quote: Track conversions, revenue, and custom events on every plan. No extra fees.

claim_b.quote: those requests will be counted as if they were pageviews

findings.why_not_just_wording: No extra fees and counted as pageviews have different consequences for the invoice.
findings.caveat: No extra fees is fair if it means no separate line item, which is true. The two statements are about 2,000 words apart on the page.

findings.headline: You say you never discount. Your help centre lists an article on discount codes.
findings.explanation: If codes exist for partners or non-profits, everyone pays the exact same price needs a qualifier.

claim_a.quote: We've never done discounts, nor will we ever.

findings.why_not_just_wording: An article about discount codes implies a way to pay less than list price, which the FAQ says does not exist.
findings.caveat: This is the weakest item here. We saw the article title in a sidebar, not its contents, and it may say you do not issue codes.

coverage_notes.what_was_not_checkable: Discovery did not reach the help articles behind the sidebar titles: Exceeding your plan limits, Billing FAQ, How do free trials work, Discount codes, and Upgrading or downgrading. Those are the pages most likely either to resolve or to worsen the findings above. Nothing we read says whether a credit card is required to begin the 7-day trial. The pricing page's slider shows one pageview band at a time, so we could only read the $45 band for 500,000 pageviews.
